23.solution:
(a) Use \(\frac{x^a}{x^b} = x^{a-b}\) and \((x^a)^c = x^{ac}\).

\(\left(\frac{x^m}{x^n}\right)^{m+n} = x^{(m-n)(m+n)} = x^{m^2 - n^2}\)

\(\left(\frac{x^n}{x^k}\right)^{m+k} = x^{(n-k)(m+k)} = x^{mn + nk - mk - k^2}\)

\(\left(\frac{x^k}{x^m}\right)^{k+n} = x^{(k-m)(k+n)} = x^{k^2 + kn - mk - mn}\)

Multiplying, add the powers: \(m^2 - n^2 + 2nk - 2mk = (m-n)(m+n) - 2k(m-n) = (m-n)(m+n-2k)\).

So the value is \(x^{(m-n)(m+n-2k)}\).

(b) \(\frac{1}{1+x^{n-m}} = \frac{x^{m-n}}{x^{m-n}+1}\) (multiply the top and bottom by \(x^{m-n}\)).

So the sum is \(\frac{1}{1+x^{m-n}} + \frac{x^{m-n}}{1+x^{m-n}} = \frac{1 + x^{m-n}}{1+x^{m-n}} = 1\).
23.why: Both passes answered 1; 1 by reading part (a)'s powers as the standard m+n, n+k, k+m. As printed (m+n, m+k, k+n) part (a) simplifies to x^((m-n)(m+n-2k)); solution rewritten for the printed version (walking-question precedent), the standard answer named in the notice.
23.notice: As printed, part (a) does not come to a number: with the powers m+n, m+k and k+n it simplifies to x^((m−n)(m+n−2k)), which is the answer worked out here. In the usual version of this question the powers are m+n, n+k and k+m, and then the value is 1.
